recipes.name: Swanny's Killer Fajitas
ingredients_raw: 2 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, cut into 1/4-inch wide strips
0.125 teaspoon cayenne pepper, or to taste
0.125 teaspoon ground black pepper, or to taste
1 red bell pepper, cut into 1/4 inch strips
0.5 cup shredded Cheddar-Monterey Jack cheese blend, divided

steps.text: Place chicken strips in a bowl and stir in lime juice, cumin, paprika, chili powder, cayenne pepper, and black pepper; marinate chicken for 15 to 30 minutes.

Heat a large skillet or wok over medium heat and pour in olive oil. Cook and stir red bell pepper and onion in the hot oil until softened, about 5 minutes; move vegetables to the outer edge of the skillet.

Place chicken strips with marinade in the center of the skillet and cook and stir until chicken is no longer pink in the center and juices run clear, about 3 minutes; cook and stir chicken and vegetables together until liquid in skillet has evaporated, about 2 more minutes. Set chicken and vegetables aside.
Place corn tortillas on a microwave-safe plate with damp paper towels separating each tortilla. Cook in microwave until tortillas are hot and flexible, about 30 seconds.
Place corn tortillas onto 4 serving plates; spread each tortilla with 1 tablespoon sour cream.
Top each tortilla with 1/4 of the chicken and vegetable mixture; sprinkle with 2 tablespoons shredded Cheddar-Monterey Jack cheese blend.
Sprinkle each tortilla with 1/4 cup lettuce and 2 tablespoons diced tomato.
Top with any other desired toppings; repeat with remaining tortillas and ingredients.

raw_recipe.headline: Swanny's Killer Fajitas
raw_recipe.description: Delicious lime-marinated chicken and vegetables are folded into hot corn tortillas and served with fresh lettuce, tomato, and sour cream. Add your favorite toppings like taco sauce, guacamole, and a sprinkle of fresh cilantro if you like.

video.description: If you like knowing a recipe that bends to the whims of what you have on hand or what you’re in the mood for, you’ll love this simple and easily adaptable recipe. Marinate strips of chicken or beef or cubes of tofu in a mixture of lime or lemon juice, cumin, paprika, chili powder, cayenne and black pepper. While that soaks up flavor, cook bell pepper and onion in oil. Warm everything together, then pile into soft corn tortillas along with sour cream, Cheddar-Monterey Jack cheese, lettuce and tomato. Adjust seasonings and vegetables to what you want and make a great meal your own.

review.reviewBody: Easy recipe and easy to tweak! Since I didn't have lime, I used lemon (lime is best but I didn't have it on hand unfortunately) - I omitted the cayenne (kids) and added garlic powder. While the chicken was marinating I started cutting up my veggies, I didn't have a red onion but yellow did just fine. Once the chicken was cooked , I tasted... it needed some salt and a little more chilli powder, cumin and garlic. AH yes that did the trick! :D IF you don't like the dryness of chicken breasts you can mix it up and cut up both chicken breasts and boneless skinless chicken thighs. YUM! Thank you for sharing this great recipe!
I gave it an upgrade. In MY OPINION you should never microwave tortillas that just leaves them slimy so I used a tortilla pan, but an iron skillet or griddle work just as well.

This is a good basic recipe for fajitas. I substituted beef sirloin for chicken. Next time I will double the marinade, because 1 lime did not generate very much juice, and I could not taste the lime at all. We like to pile on the toppings and the salsa, so this turned out pretty well despite being short on marinade.

WOW,really tasty,simple recipe. This was recipe group selection this week and I'm sure glad I made it.Since it is just hubby and me this worked out perfect.The one thing I did different was to do a combo,so I added a small sirloin steak,thinly sliced and alittle more cayenne pepper.I really liked the use of only one skillet,genius.I served with a side of Mexican rice and sliced avocadoes,and will use this recipe in our regular rotation as we love Mexican food!!Thanks Huge!

Recipe Group Selection: 03, May 2014 ~ Simple and delicious. Loved that this was a one pan deal! The marinade had very good flavor, but the next time I think I will double it, to give the meat a tad more flavor. Along with the red peppers, I add yellow, orange and green peppers. Served this with corn-on-the-cob and a fresh fruit salad. We enjoyed dinner very much. Thanks Huge, for sharing your recipe.
There wasn't enough liquid from the limes I used, so I added beer. I marinated the chicken overnight and these came out pretty good. Thanks for the recipe:)
It was good. I will try it again and brown the chicken more and add more seasoning. Added green and yellow pepper.

Enjoyed preparing this for the Recipe Group. I did enhance a bit, added more seasoning and added some smoked paprika as well. I also had a zucchini on it's last legs, so I cut into strips and added, too. Simple and delicious. Thanks for sharing your recipe with AR!

Recipe Group: This was great! Followed the recipe pretty much as stated, except my limes were teeny so I used two, and threw some lime zest in the marinade to boot. Loved the lime flavor and how the veggies got a bit of it as well. And for the record, we went through a ten pack of tortillas :) Also, juuuust realized I forgot the lettuce in the fridge :(

I had a small amount of chicken pieces so I scaled this down to two servings. I froze the chicken in the marinade and later thawed it in the refrigerator. I lost a little of the marinade to leakage so the moisture evaporated pretty much upon placing it in the pan. The flavor was subtle but good and worth marinating though it got a little lost amongst too many toppings. The lime juice came through the most upon tasting just the meat. I would perhaps add more seasoning next time but maybe not since it was quite good and we will certainly use this again. I was cooking outside so I wrapped the tortillas in foil and warmed on the grill rather than use the microwave. It only takes a minute over the gas burner.
Ok. Not as flavorful as I had hoped. If I try again will make some tweaks and then update this opinion
We really enjoyed this dish. I will definitely make this again.
This is a good basic recipe for fajitas! I actually made steak fajitas as well...Will make again for a quick dinner!
IT WAS EVERYTHING IT SAID IT WOULD BE.
This was a lot better than I expected. The flavor was very good. For a low sodium alternative, I’ll be making this again.
I loved this recipe!! Made it exactly as directed. Can't wait to make again!!
Good, but not what I'd consider fajita-tasting. 'May be my cooking, too. I followed the marinade & it was a little lime-y (not too much) &, surprisingly, not super spicy either.
Very good and easy to fix for a quick dinner provided you do the prep work ahead of time. It even pleased both of my picky sons! I will definitely make this again.
I did not care for this recipe.
